st: Put the eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water, and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat, cover, and let them sit for 10 minutes.
Move the eggs to a bowl of ice water for 5 minutes, then peel and slice them.
Spread each slice of rye bread all the way to the edges with a thin layer of the [[4 tbsp]] softened butter.
Lay the herring on four slices, then top with half of the sliced red onion, a few dill fronds, and the capers if using.
Stir the shrimp with [[3 tbsp]] mayonnaise and a squeeze of lemon, then pile onto two more slices.
Fan the sliced egg over the shrimp and the remaining two slices of bread, then add the rest of the onion and some dill.
Finish everything with black pepper and serve with lemon wedges, eating the open-faced sandwiches with a knife and fork.
Grate the onion on the fine side of a box grater into a large bowl and add the pork, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[0.5 tsp]] pepper, and the allspice if using.
Mix the pork with your hands for a minute until sticky, then stir in the egg and [[0.33 cup]] flour.
Pour in the [[0.5 cup]] milk a little at a time, mixing until the batter is loose and soft. It should be wetter than a regular meatball mix.
Rest the mixture in the fridge for 20 minutes so the flour can absorb the liquid.
Melt [[1 tbsp]] of the butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Wet a spoon and scoop oval patties about the size of an egg into the pan, flattening them lightly. Cook in batches without crowding.
Fry each patty for 5 to 6 minutes per side, adding more butter between batches, until deep golden and cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Serve warm with boiled potatoes, pickled red cabbage, or on rye bread.
Put the potatoes in a pot, cover with cold water, add [[1 tsp]] salt, and boil for 20 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Drain and keep warm.
Chop the parsley very finely. You want about [[0.5 cup]] loosely packed.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a saucepan over medium heat, whisk in [[2 tbsp]] flour, and cook for 1 minute without browning.
Pour in the [[2 cups]] milk slowly while whisking, then simmer on low for 8 minutes until thickened. Stir in the parsley, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, and the pepper.
Season the pork belly slices on both sides with the remaining salt.
Lay the slices in a cold large skillet, turn the heat to medium, and fry for 8 to 10 minutes per side until crisp and deep golden. Cook in batches if needed.
Drain the pork on paper towels and check that the pieces are cooked through.
Serve the crispy pork with the potatoes and plenty of warm parsley sauce spooned over.
Pat the pork very dry. Rub [[1 tbsp]] salt and the pepper into the meat and deep into the scored rind, which helps make crackling.
Push the cloves into the meat and tuck the bay leaves under the roast. Let it sit uncovered while the oven heats.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Set the roast rind-side up in a roasting pan and pour [[1 cup]] water around it, not over it.
Roast for 20 minutes to start the crackling, then lower the oven to 325°F (160°C).
Roast 60 to 75 minutes more, until the center reads 145°F (63°C) or higher. Add the potatoes to the pan for the last 45 minutes.
Meanwhile, melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a pot, add the red cabbage, [[0.25 cup]] vinegar, [[3 tbsp]] sugar, [[1 cup]] water, and a pinch of salt. Cover and simmer 40 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir the jelly into the cabbage at the end. Taste and add more sugar or vinegar if you like.
If the rind is not bubbly and crisp, broil the roast for 3 to 5 minutes, watching closely.
Rest the pork for 15 minutes, then slice and serve with the roasted potatoes, cabbage, and pan juices.
Put the rye kernels, sunflower seeds, and flax seeds in a bowl and cover with [[1 cup]] boiling water. Soak for at least 1 hour.
Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan with [[1 tbsp]] butter.
In a big bowl, stir the sourdough starter, buttermilk, [[0.5 cup]] lukewarm water, and molasses until combined.
Add the soaked seed mixture with its liquid, the rye flour, and [[2 tsp]] salt. Mix with a wet spoon until it forms a thick, sticky dough. It will not knead like wheat bread.
Scrape the dough into the pan and smooth the top with a wet spatula. Cover and let it rise at room temperature for 4 to 6 hours until it has grown about a third and shows cracks.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Bake for 75 to 90 minutes, until the loaf sounds hollow and reads 205°F (96°C) inside.
Turn the loaf out and cool completely on a rack.
Wrap and rest it for at least 12 hours before slicing very thinly. The crumb firms up and the flavor improves overnight.

ing: 3 tbsp melted for batter, 3 for the pan
st: Whisk the flour, [[2 tbsp]] sugar, cardamom, baking powder, baking soda, and salt together in a large bowl.
Whisk the buttermilk, 3 egg yolks, and [[3 tbsp]] melted butter in another bowl, then stir into the dry mixture until just smooth.
Beat the 3 egg whites with a clean whisk or mixer until they hold stiff peaks.
Fold the whites into the batter gently in two additions so it stays airy.
Heat an Æbleskiver pan (or a cast-iron pan with round wells) over medium heat and put a little butter in each well.
Fill each well about three-quarters full with batter. Cook for 2 minutes until the edges set.
Turn each puff a quarter turn with a skewer or knitting needle, letting uncooked batter run into the pan, and keep turning every minute until it forms a golden ball, about 5 minutes total.
Check that the centers are cooked, then move the puffs to a plate and repeat, buttering the wells again.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve warm with jam for dipping.
Whisk the flour, sugar, yeast, salt, and cardamom in a bowl. Add the lukewarm milk and 1 egg and stir to a shaggy dough.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes until smooth, wrap it, and chill for 30 minutes.
Put the cold butter between two sheets of parchment and pound and roll it into a 6-inch square. Keep it cold in the fridge.
Roll the dough into a 10-inch square, put the butter in the center like a diamond, and fold the corners over to seal it in.
Roll the dough out to a long rectangle about 8 by 20 inches. Fold it in thirds like a letter, wrap it, and chill for 30 minutes.
Repeat the roll, fold, and 30-minute chill two more times. If butter softens or leaks, chill the dough before continuing.
Roll the dough to a 12 by 16-inch rectangle and cut it into twelve squares. Put a spoonful of almond paste in the center of each and fold two opposite corners to the middle.
Set the pastries on lined baking sheets, cover loosely, and let them puff for 45 minutes at cool room temperature.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Beat the second egg, brush it on the pastries, and sprinkle with sliced almonds.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until deep golden brown. Cool on a rack.
Stir [[0.5 cup]] powdered sugar with [[1 tbsp]] water and drizzle over the cooled pastries.

ing: 6 tbsp softened for dough, 6 tbsp softened for filling
st: Mix [[3.5 cups]] flour, [[0.25 cup]] sugar, the yeast, salt, and cardamom. Add the milk, egg, and [[6 tbsp]] butter and stir until a dough forms.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and a little tacky, then put it in a greased bowl, cover, and let rise 1 hour until doubled.
Mix the remaining [[6 tbsp]] soft butter with [[0.5 cup]] brown sugar and [[2 tbsp]] cinnamon into a paste.
Roll the dough into a 12 by 18-inch rectangle and spread the filling evenly over it.
Roll up tightly from the long side into a log and cut into 12 slices. Set them cut-side up on a lined baking sheet.
Cover and let rise for 30 minutes until puffy. Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until golden brown.
Whisk [[1 cup]] powdered sugar with [[2 tbsp]] water, drizzle over the warm rolls, and serve.
Put the rice, [[4 cups]] milk, and a pinch of salt in a heavy pot and bring just to a gentle boil, stirring.
Turn the heat to low, cover, and cook for 35 to 40 minutes, stirring often to prevent sticking, until the rice is very tender and the porridge is thick.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] of the vanilla. Move to a bowl and cool to room temperature, then chill for 2 hours.
Whip the cold cream to soft peaks with the remaining [[1 tsp]] vanilla.
Fold the chopped almonds, then the whipped cream, into the cold rice pudding.
For the sauce, simmer the cherries, [[0.25 cup]] sugar, and [[0.25 cup]] of the water for 8 minutes.
Stir the cornstarch into the remaining [[0.25 cup]] cold water, whisk it into the cherries, and boil for 1 minute until glossy. Cool slightly.
Spoon the rice pudding into bowls and serve with the warm cherry sauce.

ing: or fatty pork, rind removed, chopped
st: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan with [[1 tbsp]] butter and set a baking dish of hot water large enough to hold it.
Put the liver, fatback, onion, and anchovies in a food processor and process until very smooth, scraping down the sides.
Add the egg, [[3 tbsp]] flour, [[2 tsp]] salt, pepper, and allspice, then process again.
With the machine running, pour in the [[1 cup]] milk and blend until the mixture is a loose batter.
Pour into the loaf pan and place it in the hot water bath so the water comes halfway up the sides.
Bake for 55 to 65 minutes, until firm and a thermometer reads 160°F (71°C) in the center.
Cool completely in the pan, then chill for at least 2 hours.
Slice and serve on buttered rye bread with pickled beets or cucumber.
Finely dice the half onion and slice the pickles into thin rounds.
Bring a pot of water to a bare simmer. Do not let it boil hard, or the sausages will split.
Add the sausages and heat for 6 to 8 minutes until hot all the way through.
While they heat, butter the cut sides of the buns with [[1 tbsp]] butter and toast in a skillet for 1 minute until golden.
Lay a sausage in each bun and squeeze on ketchup, mustard, and remoulade.
Top with the diced onion, pickle slices, and crispy fried onions, then serve right away.
Put the currants and [[2 cups]] water in a pot and simmer for 5 minutes until they burst. If using cranberries, simmer 8 minutes.
Add the strawberries, raspberries, and [[0.5 cup]] sugar and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Stir the cornstarch into the remaining [[0.25 cup]] cold water until smooth.
Pour the slurry into the simmering berries while stirring and cook for 2 minutes until clearly thickened and glossy.
Stir in the lemon juice and vanilla if using, then taste and add a spoonful more sugar if it is too tart.
Pour into a bowl or glasses, sprinkle a little sugar on top to stop a skin forming, and chill for at least 2 hours.
Serve cold with cold cream poured over each portion.
